stories.title: Test week: Nvidia reports Tuesday; Anthropic's debut and Korea's college exam come Thursday
stories.summary: Nvidia reports earnings on Tuesday, 17 November, its first results since Jensen Huang quit; Anthropic is expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday, the day of South Korea's college entrance exam.

stories.title: Bessent says Nvidia needs 'a dramatic shakeup' and a CEO from outside
stories.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Fox News that Nvidia's board should 'go outside the company' for its next leader, saying 'they needed a dramatic shakeup', and asked for answers within 10 days.

stories.title: A fund Ashton Kutcher co-founded could see its $435M Anthropic stake worth about $7B
stories.summary: Sound Ventures, run by Madonna's manager Guy Oseary and co-founded with Ashton Kutcher, has put $435 million into Anthropic; at the $1.4 trillion target IPO valuation its roughly 0.5% stake would be worth about $7 billion, Bloomberg reports, citing people familiar.

predictions.note: Anthropic's IPO targets a valuation of about $1.4 trillion, a trillion-dollar-scale lab valuation; the story says nothing about political leverage.

stories.title: A British trader's $10M Anthropic bet could be worth up to $3.5B
stories.summary: XTX founder Alex Gerko put $10 million into Anthropic through his venture fund three years ago; at the proposed IPO valuation it could be worth up to $3.5 billion before dilution, according to The Telegraph's calculations.

stories.title: Meituan releases a 1.6-trillion-parameter open model trained without Nvidia chips
stories.summary: Meituan released the weights of LongCat-2.5, a 1.6-trillion-parameter agent model trained entirely on Chinese hardware; it scores 88.4 on Terminal Bench v2.1 against Claude Opus 5's 89.1, by Meituan's own figures.

stories.title: Korea's top tax exam scorer confesses to cheating with AI, days before the college entrance exam
stories.summary: The top scorer on South Korea's tax accountant exam, who missed one of 160 questions, confessed to photographing them with a microcamera and getting answers from an AI tool; police are investigating, and the president's office called an emergency meeting before Thursday's college exam.

stories.title: An AI finds a hidden warning sign of sudden cardiac death in routine heart scans
stories.summary: UC Berkeley researchers, publishing in Nature, trained an AI on more than 440,000 EKGs; the group it flagged had a 7% annual sudden cardiac death rate, against 4.6% for the riskiest group standard checks found.

stories.title: Anthropic's IPO filing warns its models may take harmful actions nobody directed
stories.summary: Anthropic's prospectus says its 'A.I. models may behave in unintended, misaligned, or autonomous ways' and warns that advanced AI could pose 'catastrophic or existential risks to humanity', The New York Times reports.

stories.title: Hong Kong's airport is the first to repaint its runway lines with robots
stories.summary: Hong Kong International Airport says it is the world's first to use robots to repaint airfield markings: a centre line now takes one hour instead of three and paint savings reach HK$400,000 a year, while staff still paint the curves.

stories.title: Penn engineers build soft robot muscles that press piano keys and hold a robot's gaze
stories.summary: University of Pennsylvania engineers made artificial muscle fibres from a liquid crystal elastomer, graphene and a copper coil; a robot hand used them to press piano keys, and robot eyes used them to hold a steady gaze.

transcript.t: This is the Singularity Daily, for Monday, November 16.
Here's your day in superintelligence, in 3 minutes flat.
It's test week. Nvidia reports Tuesday. Thursday, Anthropic goes public, and Korea sits its big exam.
And Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent wants an outsider running Nvidia.
Now, the bets.
Anthropic's early backers are about to see what their bets are worth.
A fund Ashton Kutcher co-founded put in $435 million.
Its stake could be worth about $7 billion.
And a British trader's $10 million bet could be worth up to $3.5 billion.
Meanwhile, China's Meituan released a giant open AI model trained without a single Nvidia chip.
Speaking of exams. In Korea, the tax exam's top scorer missed one of 160 questions.
He confessed on Sunday: a hidden camera, an AI tool, and the answers on his phone.
He said the top score "was not the result of fair effort." Police are now investigating.
And with Korea's college entrance exam on Thursday, the president's office called an emergency meeting.
This week in Nature, Berkeley researchers trained an AI on over 440,000 heart scans.
It flagged people at risk of sudden cardi ac death that standard checks would miss.
The catch?
Anthropic's own filing warns its models could take harmful actions nobody directed.
It even warns of "existential risks to humanity." In a stock offering.
So... is it so over?
We're so back!
Back to the machines.
Hong Kong's airport is the first to repaint its runways with robots.
A centre line took three hours. Now it's one, and people still paint the curves.
And Penn engineers made soft robot muscles.
A robot hand used them to play piano.
That's test week. AI can ace the test. Passing it honestly is still on us.
Day after day, the curve keeps bending upward.
And the future keeps arriving ahead of schedule.
One day, all of this. Tomorrow, probably more.
This has been the Singularity Daily.
See you tomorrow.
Want the whole month? Hear more on November 27.
